Daniel Dubois dominates Fabio Wardley in rematch — live reaction
0
0 Comments
Link copied!
1 day ago
0
0 Comments
Link copied!
1 day ago
Mosope Ominiyi
1 day ago
8 min read
WBO heavyweight world champion Daniel Dubois promised a quicker finish and was at his destructive best, dismissing Fabio Wardley two rounds into their rematch.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:40
Instaread
Dubois (24-3, 23 KOs) scored a heavy knockdown 17 seconds into the action, just one second after Wardley (20-1-2, 19 KOs) floored him in their Manchester firefight five months earlier. That set the tone for a one-sided beatdown, against the Ipswich puncher who climbed off the canvas but only prolonged the punishment he would absorb.
All things considered, the sensible pre-fight pick was Dubois by stoppage and boy, he didn't disappoint.
The 29-year-old titleholder delivered an impressive, vicious showing to dismantle the former champion earlier than their memorable May 9 meeting, leaving Wardley with some serious questions to answer as he ponders his future.
Read Dec Taylor's fight report on location here and relive the fight night updates below...
That's all from me tonight, thanks for following along with coverage. We'll have more from Dubois, Wardley and analyst Hrgovic — who joined the DAZN broadcast — as the dust settles.
If you think we're finished for the evening, well you're mistaken! Better get some fresh air and a snack handy.
Stay tuned as Sebastian Fundora defends his WBC 154-pound title against Ermal Hadribeaj in a few hours, after former WBA 168-pound champ Armando Resendiz returns against a man living his dream in Las Vegas ...
The main card begins at 8pm ET/1am BST, live on DAZN internationally and across TNT/truTV in U.S. territories. Fancy some reading? Keith Idec's Fundora feature will get you in the mood.
DUBOIS vs. WARDLEY - ROUND 2
It's all over and destructive Dubois retains his WBO crown! 2:21 is the official time of the stoppage, Dubois improves to 24-3 with his 23rd career KO and tonight we saw a man on a mission. Devastating and determined.
Dubois is closing the distance effortlessly without expending much energy or effort, clubbing blows continue to connect cleanly... the towel comes in and Steve Gray steps in between them!
Wardley is trying to bounce and stay fleet footed, but not able to get much in the way of economical movement.
DUBOIS vs. WARDLEY - ROUND 1
Wardley's co-trainer Ben Davison reportedly has the towel in his hand... but we somehow hear the bell to end a furious first frame. Not sure this is gonna last much longer though.
The punches continue to rain down on Wardley, he does his best to hold and delay Dubois' advances but it's almost delaying the inevitable here... The swarm continues, a heavy uppercut and even more punishment persists. WOW!
Dubois has come out like he's got somewhere better to be and the roles have reversed in some style! He crunches Wardley with a whopping right hand, then more combos after Steve Gray gives the challenger a standing count... you can see IBF titleholder Filip Hrgovic watching on, among others... wonder what he's thinking here.
Queensberry's ring announcer Thomas Treiber confirms Ferenc Budai, Phil Edwards and Ammar Sakroui are the three judges ringside, though they almost certainly won't be needed here. The referee? Steve Gray.
The last men's world championship fight he officiated was Josh Kelly's 12-round upset win over Bakhram Murtazaliev in January.
Dubois is all business as he punches his gloves together, ignores marches to the ring so quickly you miss out on the song transition to a reggae number. The time for celebrations can wait, he's got business to attend to.
Wardley looks focused as tonight's challenger walks out first, manager Michael Ofo passionately rallying the troops behind him as Roy Jones Jr's Can't Be Touched song, some 22 years old, reveberates around the O2 Arena.
MAIN EVENT TIME!
Busier throughout, probably lost two or three rounds at most, though he was guilty of taking his foot off the accelerator and was duly punished. Rematch anyone? We'll have to revisit the scorecards another time because...
115-114 Gomez Jr, 114-114, 114-114 majority draw! O'Doherty retains his British and Commonwealth lightweight titles, but the challenger's reaction of pure disbelief tells you the story!
Oooooh... controversial chief support scorecard here! It's why they say don't leave it in the judges' hands...
To that end, Dubois acknowledged he was overweight first time around and guess what? He also came in heavier at 253lbs. Will speed and precision play a factor here?
You heard Hrgovic, right? I can see Wardley warming up backstage hitting pads with Rob Hodgins, but can he stay composed in the fire from arguably the sport's hardest-hitting puncher? We'll see in about half an hour's time.
Hrgovic: You can never write off Wardley
Elsewhere, an interested world heavyweight champion has shared a main event prediction to Queensberry's social channels. Hrgovic (21-1, 16 KOs) will want to avenge his own defeat by Dubois, but knows it's not that simple...
Michael Gomez is outworking him, often first to the punch, outmuscling the champion and making him work harder than he's used to.
O'Doherty finding himself having to box off the back foot and swimming upstream. Uppercuts and a stinging jab are scoring beautifully for the Mancunian, who is relentlessly walking him down. 6-1 down!
As local celebrities and notable names are being interviewed for their predictions ringside, O'Doherty has perhaps won his first round... and he's got a massive second-half to claw back here.
Chief support time... who is Ball backing in the headliner?
If you're following along, just one more fight before the main event! How about time for a prediction from a former world champion?
It's a lightweight scrap, where Louie O'Doherty (12-0, 3 KOs) defends his British and Commonwealth belts against Michael Gomez Jr (23-2, 8 KOs). Here we go then...
Olaniyan does it again!
For more on Olaniyan, read John Evans' feature piece on his time in Liverpool here.
How are you so calm? "I'm confident in my preparation, God gives me the strength to do this so I have nothing to fear. I'm ready for anything me personally, but I'll listen to the team, still serving my apprenticeship. I have the best team in the world with Queensberry, Frank Warren and ERT [Everton Red Triangle] so I'll leave it to them."
"It's what I was made for, these big nights and big events. To be on a card like this is where I wanna be in future, selling out the likes of the O2, [Liverpool] Echo Arena and Croke Park, I can't wait for the main event.
5-0 with five knockouts in just seven months as a pro, he speaks well and is picking a repeat Dubois victory in tonight's main event. During his post-fight interview with DAZN's Anna Woolhouse, he says:
Veteran heavyweight Dan Garber (14-10, 2 KOs) didn't put up resistance but Ireland's 20-year-old heavyweight prospect Adam Olaniyan dug downstairs and scored two knockdowns en route to a second-round finish.
Jalolov outboxes Dacres after Birchall's big win
It's another feather in the Uzbek's cap. While it wasn't action-packed or particularly exciting, Dacres was unlikely to truly press him enough to get the excellent amateur into a slugfest. Aggressive when he needed to be, now time for another step-up against someone who sets a pace, or at least punches hard enough to make him think more.
Final scorecards: 99-91, 99-90, 99-90: Bakhodir Jalolov (18-0, 15 KOs) bt. Solomon Dacres (10-2, 3 KOs)
The 22-year-old, who won the vacant English featherweight title with a ninth-round stoppage of Ryan Griffiths in March, will look to campaign back down in weight after coming into this one at 135 pounds.
Morecambe southpaw Nelson Birchall (13-0, 10 KOs) promised to be the first to stop Levi Giles (17-4-1, 4 KOs) and did exactly that, scoring a knockdown in three consecutive rounds before referee Sean McAvoy had seen enough.
Meanwhile there was a finish during the main card opener...
As I type this, double Olympic heavyweight champion Bakhodir Jalolov is cruising to a wide points decision against former English beltholder Solomon Dacres. They're into the eighth frame of their 10-rounder, Jalolov floored Dacres with a lethal left hand three rounds earlier and has been boxing well against the bullish Brit.
Full card results:
  • Heavy: Adam Olaniyan TKO2 Dan Garber
  • Heavyweight: Bakhodir Jalolov UD10 Solomon Dacres
  • Lightweight: Nelson Birchall TKO7 Levi Giles
  • Junior bantamweight: Tony Curtis Jr TKO4 Kerim Agius
  • Featherweight: Leighton Birchall PTS6 Alejandro Morales Chazaro
  • Lightweight: Fawas Aborode TKO4 Rashid Omar
  • Junior featherweight: Manny Safari TKO5 Jake Pollard
  • Junior light: Zayn Ahmed TKO1 Kasey Bradnum
  • Junior lightweight: Aaron Noriega TKO4 Leonardo Baez
  • Middleweight: Issiah Hamilton-Allen PTS4 Jenson Irving
If you've missed anything on a busy night of fights, never fear! Here are the full card results (updated live!)
The Ring's Declan Taylor is on site for us in the nation's capital, so stay tuned for his coverage later on. Before then though, let me take you through the results so far on the undercard...
Wardley values technique over toughness ahead rematch with Dubois
Dubois ready to turn nervous energy into chaos against Wardley
Declan Taylor: Dubois, Wardley proof that opposites do attract
Already in the running for Fight of the Year honors, both have promised adjustments. Here's some reading to get you ready for what promises to be another must-see matchup...
Five months after their instant classic in Manchester, the pair do battle once more with Dubois looking to make an emphatic first defense of the WBO world title he won at Wardley's expense last time out.
Mosope Ominiyi here and I'll be taking you through the night's action as it happens before a heavyweight rematch, exclusively live on DAZN PPV.
Welcome to The Ring's live blog commentary of Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley II.
